questions.text: A day care facility requires child-sclead toilet and lavatory fixtures. According to DSWD standards, what is the correct height for a child toilet seat (WC)?

rationale.a: 150 mm is too low for any age group.
rationale.b: 250–300 mm is the recognized child toilet seat height for day care.
rationale.c: 400 mm is adult standard, inappropriate for children; creates unsafety.
rationale.d: 600 mm is far too high for children; would require step stools, creating hazard.
rationale.correct: Child toilet seat height = 250–300 mm per DSWD standard. This accommodates toddlers and preschoolers without foot dangling.
rationale.takeaway: Child toilet seat height = 250–300 mm. Adult = 400 mm. This distinction is critical for child safety.

questions.text: A day care exit corridor must accommodate 75 children during emergency evacuation. According to PD 1096 Rule X Table X-3, what is the minimum required exit width?

rationale.b: 420 mm (0.42 m) is the mathematically correct minimum based on the 5.6 mm/person standard for doors and corridors.
rationale.c: 600 mm uses the 8.0 mm coefficient, which is reserved for stairs, not corridors/doors.
rationale.correct: Per Table X-3 of PD 1096 Rule X, exit components (other than stairs) for Group C have a width coefficient of 5.6 mm per person. 75 children × 5.6 mm = 420 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Exit width (corridors/doors) = occupants × 5.6 mm/person per Rule X. For 75 children: 75 × 5.6 = 420 mm.

questions.text: A day care facility design includes child-sclead hand-washing lavatories. According to DSWD standards, what is the correct height for a child lavatory (sink)?

rationale.a: 300–400 mm is too low and would require crawling position.
rationale.b: 550–600 mm is the recognized child lavatory height for day care.
rationale.c: 750–800 mm is adult standard, too high for children; creates accessibility barrier.
rationale.d: 900 mm is commercial counter height, not for children.
rationale.correct: Child lavatory height = 550–600 mm per DSWD standard. This enables reach and independent hand-washing for preschoolers.
rationale.takeaway: Child lavatory height = 550–600 mm. Adult = 800 mm. Proper scaling ensures independence and safety.

questions.text: Day care centers and kindergartens are classified under which occupancy group according to PD 1096?

rationale.a: Group B is residential/dormitory. Day care is NOT overnight residential; it is daytime education.
rationale.c: Group D is institutional with custodial care (hospitals, jails). Day care provides education/care supervision, not custodial institution-level care.
rationale.d: Group E is business/mercantile. Day care is educational.
rationale.correct: Day care centers and kindergartens are classified as Group C (education and recreation) per PD 1096 Rule VII. They are educational facilities, not residential or institutional custodial care.
rationale.takeaway: Day care = Group C (education/recreation). Not Group B or D.

questions.text: A day care center has activity areas accommodating 50 children during morning class. According to PD 1096 Rule X, how many emergency exits are required?

rationale.a: One exit is only permitted for occupant loads below 50 in Group C.
rationale.b: 50 occupants is the threshold where a second exit becomes mandatory per PD 1096 Rule X.
rationale.c: Three exits are only required for occupant loads exceeding 500.
rationale.d: Four exits are required for occupant loads exceeding 1000.
rationale.correct: PD 1096 Rule X Section 1007 mandates that every floor or portion thereof with an occupant load of 50 to 500 shall have at least two exits.
rationale.takeaway: Occupancy threshold = 50 persons. At 50+ = 2 exits required. Day care is subject to Rule X of the 2004 IRR.

questions.text: A day care center has 120 sqm of indoor activity/learning space. According to DSWD standards, what is the minimum required outdoor play area?

options.text: 40 sqm (one-third of indoor), which is sufficient for basic outdoor activities
60 sqm (one-half of indoor), providing ample space for various play equipment
180 sqm (1.5× indoor area), allowing for extensive outdoor play options

rationale.a: 40 sqm (one-third) is insufficient; code requires equality, not reduction.
rationale.c: 120 sqm equals indoor activity area. Meets DSWD standard.
rationale.d: 180 sqm exceeds requirement; 120 sqm is adequate.
rationale.correct: Outdoor play area must equal or exceed indoor activity area per DSWD standard. 120 sqm indoor = 120 sqm outdoor minimum.
rationale.takeaway: Outdoor play area = indoor activity area (sqm for sqm). For 120 sqm indoor = 120 sqm outdoor minimum.

questions.text: A day care facility wants to accommodate 40 children in structured activity/learning. According to DSWD standards, what is the minimum number of activity rooms required, and why?

options.text: One 60 sqm room (40 × 1.5 sqm/child), assuming no additional space is needed for other activities
Two rooms: 25 children in 37.5 sqm + 15 children in 22.5 sqm (respecting 25-child maximum per room)
Two rooms: 20 children each at 30 sqm per room (equal distribution), which allows for flexibility in room usage
Three rooms regardless of area (one per 15 children), to ensure smaller group sizes for better supervision

rationale.a: Single 60 sqm room violates the hard 25-child-per-room limit, even if total area is adequate.
rationale.b: Respects 25-child maximum while accommodating 40 total. Complies with all DSWD standards.
rationale.c: Two equal 30 sqm rooms (20 children each) works but is not the only acceptable solution; could use 25+15 distribution.
rationale.d: Three rooms unnecessary if area is sufficient; two rooms can accommodate 40 with proper distribution.
rationale.correct: DSWD mandates maximum 25 children per activity room. 40 children require minimum 2 rooms: one with 25 children (37.5 sqm) + one with 15 children (22.5 sqm).
rationale.takeaway: Activity room: 1.5 sqm/child AND max 25 children per room (hard limit). Both constraints must be satisfied.

questions.text: According to DSWD standards, what is the minimum floor area required for an activity room accommodating 20 children?

rationale.a: 20 sqm (1 sqm/child) is insufficient; DSWD standard is 1.5 sqm/child.
rationale.d: 40 sqm exceeds minimum; 30 sqm is adequate.
rationale.correct: Activity room = 1.5 sqm per child per DSWD standard. 20 children × 1.5 = 30 sqm minimum.
rationale.takeaway: Activity room = 1.5 sqm per child. For 20 children = 30 sqm minimum.

questions.text: A day care nap room is designed for 18 children sleeping. According to DSWD standards, what is the minimum required floor area for the nap room?

rationale.a: 9 sqm (0.5 sqm/child) is dangerously undersized; violates DSWD standard.
rationale.b: 16.2 sqm (0.9 sqm/child) meets lower bound of DSWD standard (0.9–1.2 sqm).
rationale.c: 21.6 sqm (1.2 sqm/child) also acceptable; uses upper bound of range.
rationale.d: 27 sqm (1.5 sqm/child) exceeds standard; activity room rate applied incorrectly.
rationale.correct: Nap room = 0.9–1.2 sqm per child per DSWD standard. Using lower limit (0.9): 18 × 0.9 = 16.2 sqm.
rationale.takeaway: Nap room = 0.9–1.2 sqm per child. For 18 children = 16.2–21.6 sqm. Lower density than activity rooms.

questions.text: A two-story day care facility has 100 sqm of activity space on the ground floor and 80 sqm on the second floor. What is the total minimum outdoor play area required by DSWD standards?

rationale.a: 80 sqm is insufficient; must account for both floors' combined activity area.
rationale.b: 100 sqm underestimates; must include second-floor activity (80 sqm).
rationale.c: 180 sqm equals total indoor activity area (100 + 80). Meets DSWD requirement.
rationale.d: 270 sqm exceeds requirement; 180 sqm is adequate.
rationale.correct: Outdoor play area must equal or exceed TOTAL indoor activity area (sum of all floors). 100 + 80 = 180 sqm indoor = 180 sqm outdoor minimum.
rationale.takeaway: Outdoor play area = total indoor activity area (all floors combined). For multi-story facilities, sum all activity areas first.
